title: Bayesian models prioritize compounds for Schistosoma mansoni assays
summary: Eight stage/time-specific Bayesian classifiers trained on historical phenotypic measurements guided prospective selection of predicted active and inactive commercial compounds. In-vitro assays reported 48% and 34% hit fractions for somules and adults, followed by triage of five compounds. The selected-set fractions are not unbiased head-to-head screening rates; no animal cure, clinical mechanism, safety or efficacy is established.

evidence.tested: Primary article reports prospective somule/adult screens and prioritized compounds after triage.
evidence.unknown: Compound-specific prior evidence and complete supplementary access remain open; no clinical inference.
evidence.ai_role: Stage/time-specific Bayesian models guided selection of assay compounds, with human curation and triage.

source_review.scope: PMC-indexed primary text; PubMed primary metadata. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
